key_terms.meaning: A set V with addition and scalar multiplication over a field F that obey ten rules: closure, associativity, commutativity, a zero vector, additive inverses, and four scalar rules with 1·v = v.
A set of scalars (R or C here) with addition and multiplication that behave like ordinary numbers, so every non-zero element has an inverse.
Scaling any vector by the scalar zero gives the zero vector; proved from 0·v = (0+0)·v = 0·v + 0·v.
The scalar −1 times v is the additive inverse of v; proved from v + (−1)v = (1 + (−1))v = 0·v = 0.
If u + w = v + w then u = v; add −w to both sides.
The set of all continuous real functions on the interval [0,1], a vector space over R under pointwise addition and scaling.
A subset W of V that is itself a vector space under the same operations; tested by: W is non-empty, closed under addition, closed under scalar multiplication.
U + W = {u + w : u ∈ U, w ∈ W}, the smallest subspace containing both U and W.
V = U ⊕ W when V = U + W and U ∩ W = {0}, so every vector of V splits in exactly one way.
A sum a₁v₁ + a₂v₂ + … + aₙvₙ with scalars aᵢ ∈ F called coefficients.
span(S) is the set of all linear combinations of vectors in S; it is the smallest subspace containing S.
S spans V when span(S) = V, that is every vector of V is a combination of members of S.
The set S is independent when a₁v₁ + … + aₙvₙ = 0 forces a₁ = … = aₙ = 0; the zero vector alone is dependent.
There is a combination giving 0 with at least one non-zero coefficient, so some member is a combination of the others.
A set that is both independent and spanning; every vector of V is then a unique combination of basis vectors.
The number of vectors in any basis of V; written dim V, and every basis of a finite-dimensional space has the same size.
The span of the rows of A, a subspace of Fⁿ; elementary row operations do not change it.
The span of the columns of A, a subspace of Fᵐ; its dimension equals the rank, and the pivot columns form a basis.
The set {x : Ax = 0}, a subspace of Fⁿ of dimension n − rank(A), called the nullity.
V/W is the set of cosets v + W with addition and scaling of cosets; dim V/W = dim V − dim W.
If V is spanned by n vectors and L is an independent set of m vectors, then m ≤ n, and basis vectors can be swapped in one at a time for vectors of L.

takeaways: A vector space is any set whose addition and scalar multiplication obey the ten familiar rules; arrows, polynomials, matrices and continuous functions all qualify.
Four shortcuts follow from the ten rules: 0·v = 0, a·0 = 0, (−1)·v = −v, and a·v = 0 forces a = 0 or v = 0.
A subspace needs only three checks: non-empty, closed under addition, closed under scalar multiplication.
The span of a set is the smallest subspace containing it, so 'does S span V' is a membership question for one vector at a time.
Independence means the zero vector has only the trivial representation; dependence means one vector is redundant.
A basis is independent and spanning, and both facts together give every vector a unique coordinate list of length dim V.
Row operations preserve the row space and the null space, while pivot columns identify a basis of the column space.
Rank plus nullity equals the number of columns, which is why a homogeneous system with more unknowns than equations has a non-zero solution.
The quotient space V/W treats vectors that differ by an element of W as one point, and its dimension is dim V − dim W.
bank_note: Long answers in this unit are mostly full proofs from the basis–dimension family plus one worked matrix problem computing row space, column space, null space, rank and nullity.

bank.q: State the ten axioms of a vector space over a field F. Using only these axioms, prove that (i) 0·v = 0, (ii) a·0 = 0, (iii) (−1)·v = −v, and (iv) a·v = 0 implies a = 0 or v = 0.
outline: List all ten axioms with symbols defined
Proof of (i) by writing 0·v = (0+0)·v and cancelling
Proof of (ii) from a·0 = a·(0+0)
Proof of (iii) from v + (−1)v = (1 + (−1))v
Proof of (iv) by dividing by a ≠ 0 using the field inverse

bank.q: Define a subspace of a vector space. State the subspace test and use it to decide whether each of these is a subspace of R³: (a) {(x,y,z) : x + 2y − z = 0}, (b) {(x,y,z) : x + y = 1}, (c) {(x,y,z) : x = 3y, z = 0}.
outline: Definition of subspace
Three-part test: non-empty, closed under +, closed under scalar multiple
Show (a) passes both closures
Show (b) fails because the zero vector is not in it
Show (c) passes and note it is a line through the origin

bank.q: Define linear combination, linear span and spanning set. Prove that the span of any subset S of a vector space V is a subspace of V, and that it is the smallest subspace containing S.
outline: Definition of linear combination with coefficients
Definition of span and of spanning set
Closure of span(S) under addition and scalar multiplication
Any subspace containing S contains every combination of S
Conclusion: span(S) is the intersection of all subspaces containing S

bank.q: Define linear dependence and linear independence. Prove that a set containing the zero vector is dependent, that a two-element set {u, v} is dependent exactly when one is a scalar multiple of the other, and that any superset of a dependent set is dependent.
outline: Definition via a₁v₁ + … + aₙvₙ = 0
Zero vector case: take coefficient 1 on 0
Two vectors: split into u = cv and c = 0 cases
Superset: extend the non-trivial relation with zero coefficients

bank.q: Define basis and dimension. Prove that if V has a basis B = {v₁, …, vₙ} then every vector of V is a unique linear combination of the members of B.
outline: Basis = independent + spanning
Existence of the representation from the spanning property
Uniqueness: subtract two representations and use independence
Definition of coordinates relative to B
Note that dim V is well defined

bank.q: For the matrix A = [[1,2,0,1],[0,1,1,1],[1,3,1,2]] over R, find a basis and the dimension of the row space, the column space and the null space. Verify the rank–nullity relation.
outline: Reduce A to row echelon form by elementary row operations
Non-zero rows of the echelon form give a row-space basis
Pivot columns of the original A give a column-space basis
Solve Ax = 0 to get a null-space basis
Check rank + nullity = number of columns

bank.q: Show that the set S = {(1,1,0), (1,0,1), (0,1,1)} is a basis of R³, and express (2,3,1) as a linear combination of the members of S.
outline: Solve the homogeneous system and show only the trivial solution exists
Independence plus three vectors in a three-dimensional space gives a basis
Solve the non-homogeneous system for (2,3,1)
State the coefficients

bank.q: Let U = {(x,y,z) : x = y} and W = {(x,y,z) : y = z} in R³. Find U + W and U ∩ W. Is R³ = U ⊕ W? Justify.
outline: Write general vectors of U and W
Show U + W contains every vector of R³
Solve for U ∩ W and get the line x = y = z
The intersection is non-zero, so the sum is not direct
Relate to dim U + dim W − dim(U ∩ W)

bank.q: State the replacement theorem. Use it to prove that any two bases of a finite-dimensional vector space have the same number of elements, and hence that dimension is well defined.
outline: Statement of the replacement theorem with the bound m ≤ n
Apply it once with basis 1 spanning, independent set = basis 2
Apply it in the reverse direction
Conclude the two inequalities give equality
Define dim V from any basis

bank.q: Let W be a subspace of a finite-dimensional vector space V. Prove that the set of cosets V/W is a vector space under the operations (u + W) + (v + W) = (u + v) + W and a(u + W) = au + W, and that dim V/W = dim V − dim W.
outline: Define cosets and the two operations
Show the operations are well defined for different representatives
Verify the ten axioms reduce to those of V
The zero element is W itself
Extend a basis of W to a basis of V and show the extra cosets form a basis of V/W

bank.q: Prove that the set of all solutions of a homogeneous system Ax = 0 in n unknowns is a subspace of Fⁿ of dimension n − rank(A), and interpret the result when n exceeds the number of equations.
outline: Closure under addition and scalar multiplication
Solve by Gauss elimination and identify free variables
Each free variable gives one basis vector
Number of basis vectors = n − rank(A)
More unknowns than equations forces a non-zero solution

bank.q: Prove that the intersection of two subspaces is a subspace but the union of two subspaces is a subspace only when one contains the other. Give an example in R² where the union fails.
outline: Intersection: zero vector lies in both, closures carry over
Union: show sum of u ∈ U and w ∈ W may leave U ∪ W
Prove the containment case is the only way the union works
Example: two distinct lines through the origin in R²
Explain why the sum of two vectors from different lines leaves the union

bank.q: Show that Cⁿ is a vector space over R and find its dimension over R. Explain what changes about dimension when the same set is viewed over C instead.
outline: Verify the ten axioms with real scalars
Show every vector of Cⁿ is a real combination of 2n vectors
Exhibit those 2n vectors as independent over R
Conclude dim_R Cⁿ = 2n and dim_C Cⁿ = n
State that dimension depends on the field, not only on the set

bank.q: State and prove the deletion theorem and the basis extension theorem for a finite-dimensional vector space. Use them to show that any independent set can be enlarged to a basis.
outline: Deletion theorem: a finite spanning set can be cut down to a basis
Proof by removing one dependent vector at a time
Dimension bound on the number of removals
Extension theorem: add vectors outside the span of an independent set
Conclusion: independent set sits inside a basis

glossary.def: An element of the field F used to multiply vectors, a real or complex number in this unit.
A set is closed under an operation when applying the operation to members of the set always gives a member of the set.
The unique vector 0 with v + 0 = v for every v in the space.
For each v there is a vector −v with v + (−v) = 0.
The linear combination in which every coefficient is zero.
The scalar multiplying a vector inside a linear combination.
A set that fails at least one axiom or one closure test, such as the first quadrant of R² under usual addition.
All polynomials of degree at most n with real coefficients, a vector space of dimension n + 1.
All m by n matrices with entries in F, a vector space of dimension mn.
The set v + W = {v + w : w ∈ W}, one point of the quotient space V/W.
The first non-zero entry of a row in the row echelon form of a matrix.
The dimension of the row space, equal to the dimension of the column space and to the number of pivots.
The dimension of the null space, equal to n − rank(A) for an n-column matrix A.
A matrix form in which each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it and rows of zeros sit at the bottom.
Row echelon form in which every pivot is 1 and is the only non-zero entry in its column.
A system Ax = 0; its solution set is always a subspace and is never empty.
An unknown of a homogeneous system that corresponds to a non-pivot column and can take any value.
The list (a₁, …, aₙ) of coefficients expressing v in a fixed basis B.
A vector space that has a finite spanning set, equivalently a basis with finitely many members.
For A with n columns, rank(A) + nullity(A) = n.
Adding new vectors to a set until it becomes a basis of the whole space.
A pairing of two vectors giving a scalar, generalising the dot product.
A length function on a vector space, written ‖v‖, obeying positivity, scaling and the triangle inequality.
